original_question: For a br-graph H, let S_H be its switching graph. A k-ary weak near unanimity polymorphism is an idempotent polymorphism phi, for k >= 3, such that phi(x, x, ..., x, y) = phi(x, x, ..., y, x) = ... = phi(y, x, ..., x, x), and it is conservative when phi(v_1, ..., v_k) is always one of the inputs. Calling a polymorphism of S_H semi-conservative when it preserves symmetric lists, is it true that S_H has a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if S_H has a conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Question 6.1(ii), with Proposition 6.2 immediately giving a negative answer.
correct_elements: Your draft already lands on the right target: it asks about the switching graph S_H of a br-graph H, uses the right polymorphism notion (weak near unanimity), distinguishes conservative from semi-conservative, and asks exactly the collapse question posed in the paper—whether semi-conservative WNU polymorphisms on S_H always collapse to conservative WNU polymorphisms.
missing_details: State explicitly that H is a br-graph (a blue-red graph) and that the question is quantified over all such H.

Define the switching graph S_H precisely, including that V(S_H)=V(H)×{0,1} and that the involution s(v,i)=(v,1-i) swaps the two copies while exchanging red and blue on the cross-copy edges as in Definition 2.3.
Define a symmetric list/subset of V(S_H) precisely as a subset A satisfying s(A)=A, where s is the switch automorphism.

Clarify that a polymorphism of S_H is called semi-conservative exactly when it preserves every symmetric unary relation (equivalently, every symmetric list), not merely some informal notion of symmetry.
Clarify that 'has a WNU polymorphism' means 'has some k-ary idempotent weak near unanimity polymorphism for some arity k>=3'; the arity is existential, not fixed in advance.
Make explicit that conservative means the value on every input tuple is one of its coordinates.
Note that the implication from conservative to semi-conservative is immediate, so the only genuinely nontrivial direction is whether semi-conservative implies conservative.

If one wants full paper-faithfulness, note that this is not one of the main conjectures from the introduction but a later polymorphism-collapse question in Section 6, and the paper answers it negatively via Proposition 6.2.
refined_question: Let H be a br-graph, and let S_H be its switching graph as in Definition 2.3, with switch involution s(v,i)=(v,1-i) on V(S_H)=V(H)×{0,1}. Call a subset A⊆V(S_H) symmetric if s(A)=A, and call a polymorphism of S_H semi-conservative if it preserves every symmetric unary relation (equivalently, every symmetric list). Is it true that S_H admits some semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism—i.e. some idempotent k-ary polymorphism for some k>=3 satisfying φ(x,…,x,y)=φ(x,…,y,x)=…=φ(y,x,…,x,x)—if and only if S_H admits some conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Fact 2.5, for every br-graph H, is the list switch-homomorphism problem LSwHom(H) polynomial-time solvable if and only if the ordinary list homomorphism problem LHom(S_H) is polynomial-time solvable?
justification: The draft does not really target the main introduction conjectures about invertible pairs, chains, and special bipartite-min orderings. Instead, it matches the later polymorphism-collapse question asked explicitly in Section 6: Question 6.1(ii) asks whether, for a br-graph H, the switching graph S_H having a semi-conservative WNU polymorphism is equivalent to S_H having a conservative WNU polymorphism. Section 2 provides the hidden definitions needed to make that question stand alone: WNU is defined in Section 2.1, the switching graph S_H in Definition 2.3, and semi-conservative in Section 2.3 as preservation of symmetric lists. The paper then immediately shows that the answer is negative by Proposition 6.2, so the paper-faithful sharpening is the exact official formulation of Question 6.1(ii), not a broader conjecture from the introduction.
